LDA is a strong, non-nucleophilic base that deprotonates the less hindered α-methyl group of the iminium ion, forming the enamine:

\[
\ce{CH3-C(=N+R2)-CH2CH2CH3 -> CH2=C(NR2)-CH2CH2CH3}
\]

The nucleophilic enamine carbon then attacks \(\ce{CH3CH2I}\), converting that α-methyl group into a propyl group. Acidic hydrolysis regenerates the ketone:

\[
\ce{CH3CH2CH2-C(=O)-CH2CH2CH3}
\]

This is **heptan-4-one**. DME serves as the solvent during the LDA step, followed sequentially by ethyl iodide and acidic hydrolysis.

Answer: C
